title: Monday, October 19: Oakdale $40 million land and water bond, District 622 referendum update, Lake Elmo elementary demolition, Stillwater assessments, county $40 million capital bonds
summary:
Oakdale Environmental Management Commission, Monday, Oct. 19, 7 p.m., Oakdale Discovery Center. $40 million proposed 2026 bond referendum. Estimated $24.60 per year for 20 years on a $420,900 median homestead. https://www.oakdalemn.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_10192026-922
Independent School District 622 Board of Education, Monday, Oct. 19, 6 p.m. 2026 referendum update and ACT testing calendar change. https://meetings.boardbook.org/Public/Agenda/1069?meeting=772292
Lake Elmo City Council public hearing, Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7 p.m., Lake Elmo City Hall, 3880 Laverne Avenue North. Demolition of old Lake Elmo Elementary at 11030 Stillwater Boulevard North. Business subsidy policy. https://www.lakeelmo.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_10202026-325
Stillwater City Council, Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7 p.m., Stillwater City Hall, 216 Fourth Street North. Assessments for street and sidewalk projects and delinquent fees. 2026 general obligation bonds. Land exchange with National Park Service. Workshop at 4:30 p.m. https://cityofstillwater.granicus.com/AgendaViewer.php?view_id=3&event_id=2010

Resolution to set November 17 public hearing for up to $40 million capital improvement bonds. $1,031,000 Byrne grant. $1,866,285.78 Axon purchase. https://www.washingtoncountymn.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_10202026-1952
script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, October 19. Here is the week's news.

Oakdale's Environmental Management Commission meets October 19 at seven p.m. at the Oakdale Discovery Center on a forty million dollar bond referendum the county is proposing for the November 3 election.

Serena Raths and Emily Jorgensen of Washington County will present on the Land and Water Legacy Program. The program was created in November 2006 with a twenty million dollar voter-approved referendum for land and water protection. Over fifty-three million dollars has been invested, nineteen million from county funds and thirty-four million from partnership funds. The proposed 2026 bonds would cost an estimated twenty-four dollars and sixty cents a year for twenty years on a median residential homestead valued at four hundred twenty thousand, nine hundred dollars. Agricultural homesteads would see three dollars per one hundred thousand dollars of taxable value. Agricultural non-homesteads would see six dollars per one hundred thousand.

Independent School District 622's board meets Monday night on a 2026 referendum update and a revision of the 2026-2027 school calendar for ACT testing.

Superintendent Tucci Osorio will give the referendum update. The agenda also lists an acknowledgment of contributions, a consent agenda with disbursements and change orders, and actions to set the time and agenda for the November 9 work study session and to set a special meeting to canvass the election. The agenda prints no dollar amounts for the referendum update or the consent items. The meeting is at six p.m. Speakers fill out a public comment sign-up sheet, state their name, and receive between two and four minutes. Public comment lasts no longer than thirty minutes.

Lake Elmo's city council holds a public hearing Tuesday on a demolition and grading permit for the old Lake Elmo Elementary and on a business subsidy policy.

Stillwater Area Schools, ISD 834, seeks to demolish the old school building at eleven thousand thirty Stillwater Boulevard North. The request covers removal of the structure, parking, drive and related improvements, earthwork, and vegetative restoration. The work would move about five hundred twenty-five cubic yards of earth per acre. The hearing also considers a business subsidy policy. The policy would set minimum requirements and standards that recipients must meet to receive a business subsidy. The hearing is at seven p.m. at Lake Elmo City Hall, thirty-eight eighty Laverne Avenue North.

Stillwater's council meets Tuesday night for public hearings on proposed assessments for street and sidewalk projects and for delinquent fees.

It will also consider a resolution for 2026 general obligation bonds, a feasibility study for the 2027 street improvement project, and a land exchange with the National Park Service. The council meets at seven p.m. at Stillwater City Hall, two hundred sixteen Fourth Street North. A workshop begins at four-thirty p.m.

Washington County commissioners meet Tuesday at nine a.m. in the County Board Room on a resolution to set a November 17 public hearing for up to forty million dollars in general obligation capital improvement bonds.

The five-year Capital Improvement Plan for 2027 through 2031 would finance the South Shop Improvements Project, Park Grove Library Improvements, and R.H. Stafford Library Improvements. The board is also asked to accept a one million, thirty-one thousand dollar Byrne Discretionary Community Project Grant for the Sheriff's Office, covering June 1, 2026, through May 31, 2030, and to approve a one million, eight hundred sixty-six thousand, two hundred eighty-five dollar and seventy-eight cent purchase order with Axon Enterprise for the period November 1, 2026, through October 31, 2031. Consent items include a two hundred fifty-four thousand, two dollar and twenty cent purchase order with Atmosphere Commercial Interiors for Law Enforcement Center furniture and a two hundred eighty-seven thousand, seven hundred forty-six dollar and sixty-two cent contract with Prevolv for Park Grove Library ancillary furniture. A later workshop covers a proposed property exchange between the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources and the National Park Service for the Fairy Falls Day Use Area and the St. Croix Boom Site Wayside, plus the South Shop project.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
